_doc:
Pre-registration record for the study protocol. The `pre_reg_lock_*` fields identify the build and schema version that this document describes; `tests/pre-reg.test.js` pins the live `src/config.js` to the `config_locked` block below so that the deployed build cannot drift from the document, and checks the thresholds in `collection_time_screen_outs` against the constants in the source. After the document is filed with a registry, any change to `config_locked` or `collection_time_screen_outs` constitutes an amendment.

The runtime config must canonicalise byte-identically to `config_locked` below; `tests/pre-reg.test.js` enforces this. Values in square brackets are placeholders that are filled in before launch (`scripts/preflight.js --strict-deployment` fails while any remain in participant-facing text).

Design revision 2026-10-24 (sampling plan). The stopping rule is now stated as one procedure: 60 completions, then top-up batches of 10 until 40 participants are retained after the three participant-level exclusion rules, with a hard maximum of 100 completions (new). The rule uses no p-values or Bayes factors. The basis of computed_n = 38 is now stated (one-df interaction, f = .25, rho = 0) and the power of the planned one-tailed t-tests at N = 40 (about .80 at d = 0.4) is recorded. Placeholders for other filters, pay amount and pay rate are filled. The study design is otherwise unchanged. This file has not been filed, so the revision is recorded here for transparency, not as an amendment.

Design revision 2026-10-24 (pattern reminders). The 4 s reminder of the gray pattern used to be due on every 8th trial of a block and was dropped whenever that trial was memory-only; with the random trial order a session got 9.6 reminders on average (4 to 14) and an imagery trial could follow the last reminder by up to 60 trials. The schedule is now planned from the trial-type sequence (src/scheduler/pattern-reminders.js): each block is cut into windows of 8 trials (pattern_phase_frequency_trials, unchanged); each window with an imagery-bearing trial (I-only, I+D or I+T) gets one reminder on one of its imagery trials; the first imagery trial of every block is always reminded; within a window the reminder goes to the imagery condition that has had the fewest reminders so far (ties: earliest), so the three conditions get near-equal exposure; and no imagery trial starts more than 9 trials (frequency + 1) after the last reminder. Memory-only trials never carry a reminder. The plan is a function of the seeded schedule (no extra randomness) and every row of a trial records pattern_reminder and trials_since_pattern_reminder. Over 500 simulated sessions this gives 15.97 reminders per session on average (15 to 16; 16 in 96 % of sessions), a longest wait of 9 trials, and per-condition counts that differ by 1.15 on average (fixed-grid alternatives: 3.6). The reminders add about 25 s per session compared with the old rule. The reminder duration, the pattern and the design are otherwise unchanged. Comparison of alternatives: scripts/pattern-reminder-montecarlo.js.

Clarification 2026-10-24 (participant-level rules and the batch tool). This file has not been filed, so this is recorded for transparency, not as an amendment. (1) Definitions, now implemented once in scripts/participant-rules.js and used by both scripts/pilot-summary.js and scripts/csv-export.js: a participant is one Prolific PID. A participant is completed if a run wrote the completion_redirect row (written when the Prolific completion link is opened) and no row of that run carries exit_reason. Data without that row is incomplete, a run that ended at a collection-time screen-out is screened out, and neither counts towards the sample size. A reload starts a new run with the same schedule; the completed run is analysed and the three participant-level rules are evaluated on that run only. A reload after main-block trials had begun is flagged (Reload_After_Main_Trials in PARTICIPANT_SUMMARY.csv) but is not an exclusion rule here. (2) instructional_attention_checks: the practice loop repeats all three checks whenever practice accuracy is below criterion. Each check counts once and counts as failed if it was failed the first time it was shown; a participant is excluded if more than 1 of the 3 distinct checks was failed (threshold unchanged). The number failed on the final administration and the number of administrations are exported beside it (PARTICIPANT_SUMMARY.csv, ATTENTION_CHECKS.csv). (3) scripts/pilot-summary.js now pools all files of a participant before it counts (it counted each uploaded file as a participant) and reads the screen-calibration outcome from the nested row value; the rule of the batch decision is unchanged. (4) The tidy tables carry star_correct_all (every planned star of the trial answered correctly, accuracy only). No table is filtered on it. Which memory-accuracy analysis is primary is not decided here. No threshold, hypothesis or design parameter was changed. 2026-10-24 (rotation, D-only, reminders). Recorded for transparency, not as an amendment. (1) The rotation angle may be 0 degrees: the six strata are now -90..-61, -60..-31, -30..-1, 0..30, 31..60 and 61..90 (built from config.grid.rotation_min_deg/max_deg), so 0 and both end points are drawn like any other angle; each stratum still holds 4 of a condition's 24 angles, 12 angles are negative and 12 non-negative, and 0 counts as non-negative in the same-sign run limit. The run limits (6 same-sign rotations, 3-degree minimum step, 6 same page background) are now also enforced across the Main A / Main B boundary; Main B is re-planned from the same seeded stream when its start cannot satisfy them. (2) D_only now goes through the same encoding code path as the imagery conditions: the grid starts upright, turns to the display angle over 500 ms and holds for 1000 ms before the first dot (it was mounted already rotated); the angle comes from the same sampler. D_only has no rotation cue and no imagination period, so its gate-to-first-dot interval is 5500 ms shorter than that of the imagery trials by design (imagery trials: cue 2000 ms + blank imagination 3500 ms + rotation and stabilisation 1500 ms; D_only: rotation and stabilisation 1500 ms only). (3) The pattern-reminder planner now chooses the placements by search over the block's windows so that the imagery conditions' reminder counts differ by at most one in every session (previously by up to five in about 4% of sessions); every other rule of the scheme (one reminder per window with an imagery trial, first imagery trial reminded, no imagery trial more than 9 trials after the last reminder, only before imagery trials, determinism from the seed) is unchanged. (4) The imagination interval is unchanged: from the end of the 2000 ms arrow cue to the first stimulus the circle with its bull's-eye is blank for 5000 ms (imagination 3500 ms + rotation 500 ms + stabilisation 1000 ms), which is the 5,000-ms imagination period of the manuscript and thesis. (5) During the arrow cue the arrow has a small transparent hole at its centre so that the bull's-eye dot stays visible. No threshold, hypothesis or other design parameter was changed. 2026-10-24 (consent and Prolific listing alignment). (1) The Prolific approval-rate filter (95% or higher) is part of the filter list, as in the first Experiment 2. (2) "Used with headphones" is no longer listed as a Prolific filter: Prolific has no such filter and the IRB-approved text says speakers are acceptable; the on-task headphone check is recorded only and never ends a session. (3) Participant-facing text no longer says that the exclusion rules are pre-registered; it says that data may be excluded under the exclusion rules of the analysis plan. (4) The screen-out payment is stated as one fixed amount ($0.14), because Prolific pays every screened-out participant the single fixed screen-out reward set on the study; the earlier statement that later exits are paid in proportion to time could not be implemented. (5) Data minimisation: the device snapshot and timing probe no longer read battery state, device memory, processor count, dark-mode, reduced-motion, forced-colours or colour-gamut preferences; nothing in this plan uses them and the consent does not name them. No threshold, hypothesis or other design parameter was changed. Clarification 2026-10-24 (final sweep; recorded for transparency, not as an amendment). (1) Headphone check: the three sounds were scheduled with a call that dropped their options, so they started together at one level; this is fixed, and the parameters now follow Woods et al. (2017): 100 ms ramps and 500 ms between the three 1,000 ms tones (they were 25 ms and 600 ms). The trial count, the pass criterion and the recorded-only status are unchanged; the kind of sound chosen on each trial and the number of anti-phase choices are now recorded. (2) Timing probe: a probe that measured no frames, or during which the tab was hidden, now fails (it passed with missing metrics); the thresholds are unchanged. (3) Music questionnaire: the Musical Training items are now the seven items of the published Gold-MSI subscale (Müllensiefen et al., 2014), with the two negatively worded items reverse-scored; the composite ranges from 7 to 49 and the absolute-pitch item stays outside it. (4) Data handling: the CSV export replaces the Prolific ID and the session id by codes (the raw uploaded files keep them and must stay private); a session without a Prolific session id gets a local id (LOCAL_..., flagged in session_id_source). (5) The exported tables no longer carry processor-count and device-memory columns. No threshold, hypothesis or design parameter was changed. Revision 2026-10-25 (final-review fixes; implementation and tooling, no threshold, hypothesis or design parameter changed): (1) The pattern-reminder totals of a whole session: the claim that the imagery conditions' reminder counts differ by at most one in every session was not true of the earlier two-step planning (Main A was planned without knowing Main B; seed fin-1197 ended 4 / 6 / 5, about 1 session in 4000). generateMainPlan now re-plans (Main B first, then both blocks, each up to 25 times from the same seeded stream) until the totals of the whole session differ by at most one, and never returns a plan that breaks the hard run limits across the Main A / Main B boundary (it throws instead). Checked on 4000 seeds (fin-0 to fin-3999): totals differ by 0 in 141 sessions and by 1 in 3859, none higher; 14, 15 or 16 reminders per session (2, 141 and 3857 sessions); no imagery trial more than 9 trials after the last reminder; reminders only before imagery trials; the first imagery trial of each block always reminded; no order-rule violation across the boundary; no generation failure. (2) Sample classes for the sampling plan: participants are classed real, pilot (is_pilot_run) or preview (no Prolific ID: a researcher opening the link without the Prolific parameters, a LOCAL_ session id). The batch decision counts real participants only (and pilot sessions only when the batch being summarised is itself a pilot batch); previews never count; every session left out is reported, and a session that has a Prolific ID but is flagged preview (a URL parameter such as SESSION_ID was missing) is counted and flagged for the researcher. PARTICIPANT_SUMMARY.csv carries Sample_Class. (3) Upload file names: a regular bucket file now carries the seq range of the rows it holds, so a bucket that grew between two upload attempts is sent again as a new file instead of being mistaken for the shorter file already stored (an identical retry is still recognised as delivered). (4) Browser support: the study needs the browsers that have Object.hasOwn, which jsPsych calls on every trial: Chrome or Edge 93, Firefox 92, Safari 15.4, or later; the page says so instead of failing at the first trial. (5) Exports: DIAGNOSTICS.csv (runtime errors and audio-state changes) and per-participant counts of them are added; free-text columns that could be read as spreadsheet formulas are protected by default (the flags --neutralise-formulas and --no-neutralise-formulas widen or switch off the protection). Revision 2026-10-25 (wave I, final consistency fixes; wording and tooling only, no threshold, hypothesis or design parameter changed): (1) The Prolific listing now has a pasted block and a researcher-only part; the two completion codes were removed from the pasted block, which participants can read before they start, and live only in the researcher-only part; prolific-study-description.md is the master and the plain-text copy beside the program is a verbatim copy. (2) The consent says the Prolific ID is stored with the responses in private research files and is replaced by a random code in the files used for analysis and sharing (the exporter does this by default). (3) Prose that quoted the tone step ratio as 1.139 (13.9 %) and three ranks as 1.48x now gives the true values, 1.138 (13.8 %) and 1.47x ((3900/200)^(1/23) = 1.1379); no config value changed. (4) study.title now equals the title of the IRB-approved consent and Prolific script. (5) Participant text: singular/plural on the redirect countdown, US spelling, 'at or above the 70% criterion' (exactly 70% passes), the pre-consent device exit no longer refers to a consent form that has not been shown, the timing-check retry text names the real cause, and the Voice on/off pill is removed when the narrated end-of-task and practice-to-main screens are left. (6) The tab-close flush no longer drops rows written between a visibilitychange flush and pagehide: pagehide is not throttled, and still sends only rows newer than the range already sent. 2026-10-26 clarification (Prolific researcher terms; no design value changed): (1) The demographics form asks only handedness, education, English fluency and glasses or contacts, plus one optional free-text note that is limited to 200 characters, tells participants not to enter identifying information, and cannot be submitted if it contains an email address, a phone number or a link. No name, email address, date of birth, age, address or phone number is requested anywhere; age and sex come from Prolific's demographic export. (2) No session ends because of an age or any other demographic answer. The only in-study exits are the device, audio and timing compatibility checks, the practice-accuracy check and consent; all other eligibility is given only through Prolific's filters, which are applied before the study is shown. (3) Eligibility conditions that no Prolific filter enforces (colour vision, cognitive impairment or traumatic brain injury) are no longer stated as self-screening requirements in the consent or the listing. (4) The earlier runs asked for a date of birth, computed an age and ended sessions on an age flag; that practice is not part of this protocol.

study.title: The Impact of Visual Imagery on Spatial Working Memory Recall: An Online Follow-up Study

design_summary.d_only_display_rotation: d_only trials show the grid rotated by display_rotation_deg (integer, -90..90, 0 allowed), drawn by the same sampler and from the same six strata as the imagery angles (-90..-61, -60..-31, -30..-1, 0..30, 31..60, 61..90) and ordered under the same run limits and minimum angle step. The grid is shown through the same encoding code path as the imagery conditions: it starts upright, turns to the angle over 500 ms and holds 1000 ms before the first dot; retention and the probes stay on the rotated frame. D_only has no rotation cue and no imagination period.

hypotheses.label: Dual-task cost (visual modality)
hypotheses.equivalence_test: TOST with d_bound = 0.1 if the directional test fails.

hypotheses.label: Modality specificity (Modality × Load interaction)
hypotheses.claim: The 2 (modality: dots, tones) × 2 (load: single, dual) within-subjects interaction discriminates a modality-general account (similar ΔAccuracy) from a visuo-spatial-specific account (greater I+D cost).
hypotheses.test: Bayesian model comparison with default JZS prior r = sqrt(2)/2 (≈ 0.707). Decision rule: BF10 > 3 supports interaction; BF01 > 3 supports null (modality-general).

hypotheses.label: Symmetric imagery cost
hypotheses.claim: Star accuracy in I+D < I_only AND I+T < I_only.
hypotheses.test: Two one-tailed paired t-tests; both must reach α = 0.05.

hypotheses.label: On-letter facilitation replicates and is amplified under dual-task
hypotheses.claim: Within memory-bearing conditions, accuracy(T_on) > accuracy(T_off); the on/off effect is larger when imagery is concurrent (I+D, I+T) than in single-task (D_only, T_only).
hypotheses.test: Repeated-measures ANOVA on probe_type × concurrency, with planned contrast on the interaction.

exploratory_analyses: Star × probe-type contingency: does dual-task release happen more cleanly when star is off the cell of the upcoming probe?

Strategy × dual-task cost: pre-registered Spearman rho on the Structural Chunking composite (strategy_q01 + strategy_q02 + strategy_q03, range 3–15) against per-participant ΔAccuracy (single − dual), separately for I+D and I+T.

Imagery-maintenance composite × accuracy: Spearman rho on imagery_maintenance_id (strategy_q13 + strategy_q15, range 2–10) against I+D star accuracy, and imagery_maintenance_it (strategy_q16 + strategy_q18, range 2–10) against I+T star accuracy — construct-validity check that endorsement of continuous-visualization / phase-specific-focus tracks the imagery-maintenance manipulation.
Strategy-questionnaire item-level Spearman screening across the 19 items (5-point Likert) against overall accuracy and ΔAccuracy.

sampling_plan.recruitment_counts: Completed sessions: participants who finish the whole session and submit the study completion code. Screen-outs (they receive the screen-out completion code), returns and time-outs do not count; their Prolific places are replaced by raising the study's place count.
sampling_plan.retained_definition: A completed session that is not excluded by any of the three participant-level analysis rules in exclusion_rules: screen_calibration_inconsistent, instructional_attention_checks, single_task_floor. The trial-level rules (display_guard_flags, rt_cutoff) drop trials, not participants, and do not enter the retained count.
sampling_plan.stopping_rule: Recruit until 60 participants have completed the session. Apply the three participant-level exclusion rules to every completed session and count the retained participants. If retained N >= 40, stop recruiting. If retained N < 40, recruit one more batch of 10 completions, re-apply the rules to all sessions and recount; repeat until retained N >= 40 or 100 participants have completed the session, whichever comes first. All retained participants from every batch are analysed (nobody is dropped to equalise N). If 100 completions are reached with retained N < 40, recruitment stops and the confirmatory results are reported as underpowered.
sampling_plan.no_optional_stopping: Whether another batch is recruited depends only on the retained count, which is computed from the participant-level exclusion rules. It never uses p-values, Bayes factors, effect sizes or any contrast between conditions, so no p-value-based or Bayes-factor-based optional stopping is used. The single_task_floor rule uses accuracy in the two single-task conditions only.

prolific_setup.note: Places taken by screen-outs are replaced so that completions, not submissions, reach the target. The hard maximum is a budget cap, not a power-based quantity.

sampling_plan.batch_decision_tool: scripts/pilot-summary.js reports completed, retained and the next step (collect, recruit a batch, stop, or stop at the maximum) from the sampling_plan numbers in this file.

power_analysis.computed_n_basis: Smallest N with power >= .85 for the one-df Modality x Load interaction of the 2 x 2 within-subjects design (m = 4 repeated measurements): Cohen's f = .25, alpha = .05, noncentrality lambda = f^2 * N * m / (1 - rho) with rho = 0 (no correlation among the repeated measures; conservative), df = (1, N - 1). G*Power's default rho = .5 would give N = 20 and rho = .3 would give N = 28. Reproduced by pre-reg/power-analysis.py.

confirmatory_t_tests.tests: H1, H2 and the two tests of H4: one-tailed paired t, alpha = .05, smallest effect of interest d = 0.4
confirmatory_t_tests.note: The retained minimum of 40 gives about .80 power for each directional test at d = 0.4, not .85; the interaction in computed_n is the test powered at .85. The joint power of the two H4 tests is the product of two such powers if they are independent.

prolific_prescreeners: Vision: normal or corrected-to-normal vision (glasses or contacts)
Device: a desktop or laptop computer
filters.other_filters: None beyond the Prolific prescreeners listed above (which include the Prolific approval-rate filter, 95% or higher). The recruitment script approved by the IRB also names filters for country of residence, first language, colour vision, cognitive impairment, dyslexia and ADHD; those are not part of this list.
filters.note: Eligibility is determined only by the Prolific prescreeners above; the study does not test age, hearing or vision.

compensation.pay_rate_per_hour: about $14 ($26 for an estimated 110 minutes is $14.18 per hour)

participant_pay_budget_usd.excludes: Prolific service fees and the $0.14 screen-out payments

compensation.payment_for_screened_out_time: A fixed screen-out payment of $0.14 through Prolific, the same whichever check ends the session.

rules.rule: A trial whose row has a non-empty `guard_flags` is dropped from analysis. `guard_flags` lists the display-guard events since the previous trial (zoom change, fullscreen exit, resize, tab hidden or visible, window blur or focus, --mm reset, pause, resume).
Participants whose screen calibration outcome is `inconsistent_accepted` (the two card settings of the last attempt differ by more than the consistency tolerance but were accepted) are excluded.

Fails > 1 of the 3 typed-instruction attention checks (strict greater-than; equality at threshold is not exclusion). Each check counts once: it counts as failed if it was answered incorrectly the first time it was shown (the practice loop repeats all three checks); the number failed on the final administration is exported beside it.
Overall recognition accuracy <= 0.55 in EITHER D_only OR T_only single-task condition.
Per-trial RT < 250 ms is treated as anticipatory and excluded from RT analyses (logged but not enforced at collection).

exclusion_rules._doc: Rules applied at analysis. Checks that end a session at collection are listed separately under `collection_time_screen_outs`.

collection_time_screen_outs._doc: Checks that end a session during data collection. They are task-capability checks, not eligibility screening, and are disclosed in the consent form. A participant who fails one is shown an explanation and sent to Prolific with the screen-out completion code; the rows collected so far are uploaded first. Thresholds are the constants in the source files named in each entry.

rules.rule: A phone or tablet is detected from the user agent (iPhone, iPod, iPad, iPadOS reporting a Macintosh user agent with more than one touch point, Android, other mobile user agents), or the device has neither hover nor a fine pointer.

rules.when: after consent, demographics, viewing-distance and display-mode screens
rules.rule: Two card-width settings per attempt (one starting low, one high, random order), up to 3 attempts. An attempt is usable if both settings moved the slider, px per mm lies in the bounds and the implied screen width lies in the bounds. A usable attempt is accepted if the two settings agree within the tolerance; a usable but inconsistent attempt is accepted only on the last attempt and flagged. If no attempt is accepted the session ends.

rules.when: after the volume instruction and fullscreen
rules.rule: The tone sweep plays up to 10 times; if the participant never reports the tones as clearly and comfortably audible, the session ends.
6 trials (three 200 Hz tones, say which is quietest); passing is 5 or more correct. Recorded as `headphones_pass`; never ends the session.

8 trials with two adjacent tones of the bank at the participant's playback level; 7 or more correct is required. One retry after a prompt to raise the volume; a second failure ends the session. A further block of 8 trials 12 dB lower is recorded only.

rules.when: after the pitch check, in fullscreen
rules.rule: Frame timing and timer accuracy are sampled; the check fails if any threshold below is violated, if no frame metrics could be obtained, or if the tab was hidden during the probe. One retry after a prompt to close other programs; a second failure ends the session.
Cumulative practice accuracy must reach the criterion; one repeat of the whole practice is allowed (2 attempts). Failing the second attempt ends the session.
If the zoom or fullscreen change cannot be restored, the pause overlay offers an end-the-session button after 30 s; using it ends the session. The guard is switched off after the last trial.

counterbalance_invariants.claim: On/off-pattern membership computed from gray_pattern = [1,2,3,7,10,11,12,13,14,17,21,22,23] minus centre cell 12; 12 on-pattern + 12 off-pattern non-centre cells.

Every single-task (D_only, T_only, I_only) trial places open-square dummies at the slot positions the matched dual-task condition uses for its other modality, and each dummy slot runs on the envelope of the event it stands in for: D_only and T_only dummies stand in for the matched I+D / I+T star and run on the S-slot envelope (3000 ms + 500 ms), while I_only dummies stand in for the matched I+D / I+T memory item and run on the M-slot envelope (1000 ms + 500 ms). Total slot count per trial and total encoding-window duration are therefore identical between each single-task condition and the dual-task condition it stands in for.

Run-length cap = 2 for memory-vs-star sequencing within a dual-task trial. For each 24-trial condition block, 24 sequences are drawn (with replacement) from the 14 valid length-6 binary strings (3 zeros + 3 ones, no run > 2), with the added constraint that each of the 6 slot positions hosts M on exactly 12 trials and S on exactly 12 trials. There are 14 valid length-6 strings, so the 24 sequences of a block are drawn with replacement; the slot-position 12/12 balance is enforced by construction in `src/scheduler/within-trial.js`.

Across 24 trials of a given memory-bearing condition, each of {T_on, T_off, F_on, F_off} appears exactly 18 times (72 probes / 4 = 18), with each probe serial position receiving six instances of each type. In the dual-task conditions, each encoding-position-to-probe-position mapping (3 encoding positions × 3 probe positions = 9 cells) appears exactly 8 times.
Across the 24 trials of any condition, each of the 6 within-trial slot positions hosts a memory-item position on exactly 12 trials and a star-or-placeholder position on exactly 12 trials.

Across each 24-trial memory-bearing condition, 36 encoded memory items are on-pattern and 36 are off-pattern, and each of the three encoding positions receives exactly 12 on-pattern and 12 off-pattern items.
Across each 24-trial imagery-bearing condition, 36 stars are on-pattern and 36 are off-pattern, and each of the three star serial positions receives exactly 12 on-pattern and 12 off-pattern stars.
Run-length cap = 2 for trial-type interleaving across the block.

In each 24-trial condition with a rotation (I_only, I_D, I_T imagery angles and D_only display angles) the angle is a whole number of degrees in -90..+90 (0 and both end points allowed, drawn at random) from six strata (-90..-61, -60..-31, -30..-1, 0..30, 31..60, 61..90; built from config.grid.rotation_min_deg/max_deg), 4 per stratum, no angle repeated within a condition, 12 counter-clockwise (negative) and 12 non-negative (0 or clockwise); 0 degrees occurs in 4/31 of the conditions' draws. In a main block the trials of one condition are reordered among themselves so that, over all rotated trials and across the Main A / Main B boundary, no more than 6 consecutive rotations have the same sign (0 counts as non-negative), consecutive angles differ by at least 3 degrees and the page background does not repeat more than 6 times in a row. D_only display angles are drawn after all other draws of the D_only block, so the other counterbalance draws do not depend on them.

Every counterbalance step consumes from a single Mulberry32 PRNG seeded from a hash of the string PROLIFIC_PID|STUDY_ID|SESSION_ID (a random preview string when the URL has no Prolific parameters). The seed string and its 32-bit hash are stored in the data (`prng_seed_string`, `prng_seed_uint32`), so the schedule of a session can be rebuilt from its seed. Different participants get different schedules; the same URL parameters (a reload of the same session) give the same schedule; a new Prolific session of the same participant gets a new one.
counterbalance_invariants.tested_in: tests/main-blocks.test.js (reproducibility from same seed; divergence under different seeds) + tests/design-montecarlo.test.js

counterbalance_invariants.claim: In every T_only and I_T trial the three encoded tones are at least 3 ranks apart in the 24-tone bank (rank = bank index + 1; neighbour ratio ≈ 1.138, so 3 ranks ≈ 1.47×), and every foil probe tone is at least 3 ranks from every encoded tone of that trial; targets are the encoded tones. The rule applies only to tones: D_only and I_D choose dot cells without any spatial-distance rule, so a foil dot may fall in a cell next to an encoded dot.

Every 24-trial condition has exactly 12 white-background and 12 light-gray-background trials, and each 12-trial half (Main A, Main B) of every condition has exactly 6 of each; over presentation order no more than 6 consecutive trials share a background.

data_record.claim: Every per-trial data row written by the runner validates against schemas/trial.schema.json (the per-row JSON Schema). Phase tags listed in the schema's `phase` enum are exhaustive — adding a phase requires editing both the runner emitter and the schema.
data_record.csv_export_compatibility: Analysis scripts read column conventions from `Ast_*`, `Dot_*`, `Qmark_*` and `Mid_Q_*` prefixes. The CSV export transforms the per-row JSON to those columns; it is not pre-registered (it is a downstream transform of the locked raw record).

strategy.instrument: Strategy questionnaire — 19 items adapted from a longer instrument; items written in the pattern/star/circle/tone vocabulary of this study and selected under retention rules (a) |ρ| ≥ .30 with accuracy or dual-task cost at p ≤ .075, (b) component of the GLM-validated Structural Chunking composite, (c) theoretical centrality to imagery maintenance; 5 items for the tone-only and image+tone conditions (Pitch Labeling, Auditory Imagery, Contour Encoding, Tonal Chunking, Concurrent Auditory Rehearsal) anchored in Dowling (1978), Hubbard (2010), Williamson et al. (2010), and Logie (1995); 1 rotation item (Probe Rotation Alternative; Cooper 1975 / Carpenter & Just 1985).
strategy.scale: 5-point agreement Likert; 1 = Strongly disagree, 5 = Strongly agree

composites.structural_chunking_composite: sum(strategy_q01, strategy_q02, strategy_q03); range 3-15; GLM-validated predictor (β = 0.415, z = 7.68, p < .001)
composites.imagery_maintenance_id: sum(strategy_q13, strategy_q15); range 2-10; Continuous Visualization + Phase-Specific Focus, I+D condition
composites.imagery_maintenance_it: sum(strategy_q16, strategy_q18); range 2-10; same constructs applied to the new I+T condition for cross-modal generalisation

attention_checks.format: typed single-word response, normalised by trim+lowercase (no punctuation strip)
attention_checks.comparator: strict greater-than (failed > max_failures triggers exclusion; equality does not)
attention_checks.session_termination: no — failed participant completes the session and receives full pay; the flag is recorded for analysis-level exclusion only

open_questions_at_lock_time._doc: These items are deliberately NOT pinned in the `config_locked` snapshot because they require researcher-side decisions before filing. Each is tracked as a deployment-readiness item, not a methodological undecidable.
